verdict.line: You lose if you let him land E (Death's Grasp) and trade freely into his sustain; you win if you poke with Q and deny his passive stacks before all-ins.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser's W (Indestructible) banks damage from both dealing and taking hits into a shield he converts to healing, so straight trading just refunds his sustain. The matchup's 48.3% win rate over 2840 games reflects that Malphite has no tool to stop the E (Death's Grasp) pull into a stacked Q (Obliterate), and his own E (Ground Slam) scales off Armor he hasn't built yet at level 1-3.

theirWindow.when: E (Death's Grasp) off cooldown, you're near minions
theirWindow.what: He will pull you in with Death's Grasp and follow with Obliterate; stay outside 700 range when his E is up so he can't chain the pull into stacked Q damage.

yourWindow.when: His E (Death's Grasp) just went down
yourWindow.what: Use Q (Seismic Shard) to poke and slow his retreat for free poke damage, since without the pull he has no way to force extended exchanges on you.

start.why: The extra regen and block-on-hit sustain directly counters his poke-heavy Obliterate trades and the 48.4% win rate on Doran's Ring data shows most lanes skip sustain items you actually need here.

boots.why: Magic resist and tenacity reduce his all-in damage and the duration of any crowd control he lands through Death's Grasp.

core.why: Early Armor and magic resist directly scale your E (Ground Slam) damage while giving sustain against his magic poke.
Armor and damage reflection punish his melee autos and Obliterate casts in extended fights.
Armor plus attack speed reduction on him weakens his ability to stack Darkness Rise passive quickly.

situational.when: he is building burst magic damage and you need a shield that blocks a Realm of Death all-in
you are ahead and want to apply extra pressure through wave clear and prolonged skirmishes

runes.keystoneWhy: The sustain and max-health damage proc rewards trading on cooldown without needing to all-in, which matters since Mordekaiser's W punishes aggressive extended fights.

summoners.why: Teleport lets you reset after losing early trades and return with full resources, while Flash is your only way to dodge a Death's Grasp pull or reposition out of Realm of Death range.

playing.title: Poke, don't trade
playing.detail: Use Q (Seismic Shard) at range whenever it's up since prolonged melee trades feed his W (Indestructible) shield on both ends.

playing.title: Track E cooldown before auto-trading
playing.detail: Death's Grasp has a 16/14/12/10/8s cooldown; never stand in a position where the pull plus his Obliterate can combo you before level 6.

playing.title: Respect level 6 all-in
playing.detail: Once Realm of Death is up, he can commit to extended fights knowing he keeps your stats on a kill; play passive near his 6 if you're even on HP.

playing.title: Save W for his engage, not yours
playing.detail: Brutal Strikes' armor and AD buff is best used reactively when he commits E into you, not as an opener, since you want the trade to happen on your terms.

playing.title: Freeze when behind
playing.detail: If you lose the early trades, freeze the wave near your turret to deny him easy E-Q combos on minions and champion together.

playing.title: Build Armor before damage
playing.detail: Ground Slam's damage scales off your Armor stat, so Hollow Radiance and Thornmail aren't just defensive—they're your main damage scaling against him.

playing.title: Don't walk into Death's Grasp range for last hits
playing.detail: 700 range covers most of the wave; step up only when his E is confirmed down or you bait it out first with Q poke.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, and summoner spells are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1); the matchup reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own tactical read, not sourced from the win-rate data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid fighting Mordekaiser head on as well as being pulled by his (E). Use [Q] to focus on contesting and farming lane.
